<a id="ambient-motion"></a>

## Ambient motion

# Ambient motion

Ambient (decorative) motion moves without input. It sets a mood, but it competes for attention and never stops on its own.

Rules: keep it slow, use it once per page, and give it an off switch. Moving content that lasts more than five seconds needs a way to pause it (WCAG 2.2.2), and it must respect [[reduced-motion]].

[[orbit-animation]] is ambient motion. It becomes an interaction once it responds to the visitor, for example by pausing on hover.

<a id="counter-rotation"></a>

## Counter-rotation

# Counter-rotation

When a parent rotates, its children rotate with it. To move something around a circle while keeping it upright, rotate the child the opposite way at the same speed. The two cancel out.

[[orbit-animation]] runs the same [[css-keyframes]] animation in `reverse` on each planet, so labels always read normally.

<a id="css-custom-properties"></a>

## CSS custom properties

# CSS custom properties

Custom properties (`--name: value`) are variables that cascade like any CSS property. JavaScript can set them on an element, and CSS can use them anywhere below it.

This splits the work cleanly. In [[3d-tilt-hover]], JavaScript sets `--tilt-rx` and `--tilt-ry` and the stylesheet owns the transform. In [[orbit-animation]], one variable, `--orbit-play`, pauses every animation at once.

Patterns in this library style themselves through custom properties, so a product's own colors and spacing can replace the defaults.

<a id="css-keyframes"></a>

## CSS keyframes

# CSS keyframes

`@keyframes` names an animation and its steps. The `animation` property runs it on an element, with a duration, a timing function and a repeat count.

The browser runs it without JavaScript, often off the main thread. [[orbit-animation]] uses one `orbit-spin` keyframe for every ring, and [[counter-rotation]] runs the same keyframe in reverse.

<a id="custom-hook"></a>

## Custom hook

# Custom hook

A custom hook is a function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other hooks. It lets several components share behavior without sharing markup.

`useTilt()` holds all the pointer math and the animation loop for [[3d-tilt-hover]], and returns a ref. Any element that takes the ref can tilt. It pairs with [[refs-over-state]] to stay fast.

<a id="decorative-aria-hidden"></a>

## Decoration and aria-hidden

# Decoration and aria-hidden

Some elements exist only to look good: a glare, a moving planet. A screen reader reading each of them adds noise.

Two options. Hide decoration with `aria-hidden="true"`. Or, when the visual carries meaning, give the whole thing one description with `role="img"` and an `aria-label`, and hide the parts.

[[3d-tilt-hover]] hides its glare. [[orbit-animation]] is announced as one image when it has a label, and is hidden entirely when it does not.

<a id="usesyncexternalstore-media-query"></a>

## Media query hook

# Media query hook

`useSyncExternalStore` subscribes a component to a value that lives outside React. A media query is exactly that: the browser owns it and fires `change` when it flips.

`usePrefersReducedMotion()` subscribes to `(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and returns a boolean. Components re-render when the visitor changes the setting, with no effect or state of their own.

It is the React side of [[reduced-motion]]. Used by: [[3d-tilt-hover]], [[orbit-animation]].

<a id="pointer-events"></a>

## Pointer events

# Pointer events

Pointer events (`pointermove`, `pointerdown`, `pointerleave`, `pointercancel`) fire for mouse, pen and touch alike, so one set of listeners covers every input.

`pointercancel` matters on touch: it fires when the browser takes over, for example to scroll. [[3d-tilt-hover]] listens for it and eases the card back to flat.

Touch has no hover. A pointer-driven effect needs a plan for touch, such as reacting only while a finger drags.

<a id="reduced-motion"></a>

## Reduced motion

# Reduced motion

People who get dizzy or distracted by movement can ask their operating system for less of it. The browser exposes that as the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media query.

Every animation in the library has a still version. In CSS, check the media query. In React, read it with a hook that subscribes to changes (see [[usesyncexternalstore-media-query]]), so the page updates if the setting changes while it is open.

The still version should keep the meaning, not just stop. A tilt card stays flat but keeps its subtle lift. An orbit holds its planets in place so the labels stay readable.

Used by: [[3d-tilt-hover]], [[orbit-animation]].

<a id="refs-over-state"></a>

## Refs over state

# Refs over state

React state re-renders a component every time it changes. For values that change 60 times a second, such as a rotation angle, that is wasted work.

Instead, keep a ref to the element and write the value directly, usually as a [[css-custom-properties]] value. React renders once; the animation loop ([[requestanimationframe]]) updates the DOM.

Used by: [[3d-tilt-hover]].

<a id="requestanimationframe"></a>

## requestAnimationFrame

# requestAnimationFrame

`requestAnimationFrame` calls a function just before the browser paints the next frame. Calling it again from inside that function makes a loop that runs once per frame.

A good loop stops itself when nothing is moving. [[3d-tilt-hover]] eases toward its target a little each frame and stops once the card is still, so an idle card costs nothing. Values go to the DOM through [[refs-over-state]].

<a id="web-animations-api"></a>

## Web Animations API

# Web Animations API

`element.getAnimations()` returns the animations running on an element, including ones started by CSS. Each one has `currentTime` and `playbackRate`.

Changing `animation-duration` mid-flight makes things jump. Changing `playbackRate` changes speed smoothly, and a negative rate plays backwards. [[orbit-animation]] uses it for its speed and direction controls.
